title: Measuring the Nerve Fibre Layer

patient.name: Mdm Tan Hwee Cheng
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for an RNFL OCT scan to monitor her glaucoma

history.hpc: Mdm Tan is a glaucoma patient referred for a peripapillary RNFL OCT for monitoring. She says: 'My doctor want to check my nerve, see got thinning or not.' She is on glaucoma drops and attends regularly. No new symptoms. The OT must acquire a well-centred RNFL scan and document for comparison with previous scans.
history.pmhx: Primary open-angle glaucoma, both eyes. Hypertension.
history.social_hx: Lives with husband. Compliant with drops and follow-up. Non-smoker.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Clear media; optic discs show glaucomatous cupping (known)
examination_findings.fundus: Glaucomatous optic discs; RNFL OCT to quantify and monitor — for doctor review

investigations.rnfl_oct: Peripapillary RNFL OCT acquired both eyes. Scan centred on the optic disc with the measurement circle correctly placed; good signal strength and stable fixation confirmed. Findings show inferior RNFL thinning, more on the right, consistent with glaucomatous loss. Saved for comparison with prior scans.
investigations.scan_quality: Disc-centred, measurement ring well-positioned, signal strength adequate, no major motion artefact.

diagnosis: RNFL OCT shows inferior RNFL thinning consistent with glaucoma, useful for monitoring progression against previous scans. The OT competency is correct disc-centred acquisition, quality control, and documentation for trend comparison; interpretation is the doctor's.

immediate: Confirm the indication (glaucoma monitoring) and which eye(s) to scan
Position the patient and ensure the scan is centred on the optic disc with the measurement circle correctly placed
Confirm good signal strength and stable fixation; re-acquire if decentred or motion-degraded
Acquire RNFL scans for both eyes
Document diagnosis, indication, eye(s), and findings, and ensure it can be compared with prior scans
Avoid interpreting beyond quality control — present for doctor review
follow_up: Doctor to compare RNFL with previous scans to assess progression
Continue glaucoma drops and monitoring as scheduled
Save the scan for serial comparison
patient_education: Explain the scan is a painless light scan to measure the nerve fibre layer
Ask her to keep still and look at the fixation light
Explain the doctor will compare with previous scans to see if the glaucoma is stable
Reinforce the importance of continuing her drops and follow-up
